llm.summary: FounderClaw is a disclosed multi-agent/browser automation system, but its installer and local browser-control service expose enough high-impact authority that users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The browser daemon binds to localhost, but artifact code returns the bearer token from unauthenticated /health, exposes browser refs/activity without authentication, and routes cookie picker discovery/import before the general auth check.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README and installer support piping a mutable GitHub main-branch script directly to bash, cloning/updating from main, running bun install without a lockfile present, and compiling local executables.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package asks the user to run broad install/update commands that symlink many skills, modify OpenClaw configuration, add agent behavior, and reset the installed repository to origin/main; some paths are interactive in docs, but the shell installer performs major mutations without an explicit per-step confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The system persistently installs skill symlinks, workspace files, OpenClaw agent config, session/log files, and can launch background browser and sidebar-agent processes; much of this fits the stated purpose, but the scope is broad.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent: it installs a multi-agent OpenClaw workflow, browser testing skills, a workspace, and optional authenticated-browser QA support. Browser control and cookie import are disclosed, but they are inherently sensitive capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a broad local agent system that modifies OpenClaw configuration, runs a browser daemon, and can use authenticated browser sessions. Prefer cloning and reviewing a pinned commit instead of using curl | bash, avoid importing cookies on shared or untrusted machines, and do not leave the browser daemon running while handling sensitive web accounts.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Cookie and Keychain access is expected for the setup-browser-cookies feature and is disclosed, while the .env references are development/security-audit examples rather than evidence of credential theft.
[TM2] unexpected: The curl-to-bash installer from a mutable main branch is artifact-backed and unnecessarily collapses download, review, and execution into one step.
[RA1] expected: The self-update capability is disclosed as founderclaw-upgrade, but it uses git reset --hard origin/main and broad re-symlinking, so users should treat updates as high-impact.
[TP4] expected: The uninstaller removes FounderClaw symlinks, its repo, and agent config while preserving the workspace; this is expected uninstall behavior, not malicious by itself, but it should be confirmed before use.
[T03] unexpected: The remote installer execution concern is supported by README.md and install.sh and remains a material install-chain risk.
[T05] unexpected: Cookie picker routes are explicitly unauthenticated in code while they enumerate browser profiles/domains and can import decrypted cookies into Playwright.
[T09] unexpected: The local browser service discloses AUTH_TOKEN via unauthenticated /health and exposes browser URL/activity metadata on unauthenticated wildcard-CORS endpoints.
[T08] unexpected: The installer runs bun install against caret dependency ranges and no lockfile was found in the inspected tree, making installs less reproducible.
